newsitem.title: TAIWAN: CHINA GRAIN - U.S. SOYBEAN RALLY KEEPS CHINA AWAY.
newsitem.headline: CHINA GRAIN - U.S. SOYBEAN RALLY KEEPS CHINA AWAY.

text.p: Chinese buyers are expected to remain out of the U.S. soybean market following the sharp rally in Chicago futures prices, oilseeds traders said on Thursday.
"Chinese buyers have not been buying since Tuesday's USDA reports triggered soaring corn and soybean prices," a Shanghai-based grain trader said.
Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) soybeans jumped on Wednesday on tight near-term supplies, with August settling up 35-1/4 cents at US$7.79 per bushel.
Some Chinese traders described Wednesday's soybean rally as "crazy" and said buyers would not enter the market at a time of high uncertainty.
"A surge of more than 30 U.S. cents in one day is crazy," a Chinese trader said. "Chinese buyers will stay out until the market settles down."
Buyers would be willing to buy U.S. soybeans at about $265 a tonne C&F, which compares with current indications between $275 to $280, she added.
"Some U.S. soybean shipments were bought at $260 a tonne, so buyers don't want to buy nearby shipments at higher prices."
Traders said Chinese buyers are seeking some U.S. soyoil, but volumes remains small due to the state import limits.
"There are some people asking for soyoil, but the limited government import quotas are keeping the actual buying thin," a trader said.
The Chinese corn market is also fairly quiet. Some Japanese buyers are considering purchasing Chinese corn, but are looking for a price of around $123 a tonne C&F, traders said.
This compares with offers from Chinese traders at between $125-$128 a tonne C&F, up from $122-$124 before the surge in the Chicago market on Tuesday, they added.
China itself is unlikely to import corn this year due to ample levels of government stocks, traders said.
